text:
claire: FYI the optkit migration PR (#4823) failed the linkcheck and the sample snippets for batching + kv-prefetch + quant profiles are missing. can someone pick up a quick patch? :grimacing:

samir: I can take the snippets. do we want one consolidated example showing both Python and Go SDK usage, or split per language?

claire: consolidated but short. goal = a small end-to-end recipe: 1) enable batching, 2) enable kv prefetch, 3) apply a quant profile for latency-sensitive inference. call out tradeoffs.

leo: also the migration guide needs a short checklist (breaking changes) and a link to the quant profiles table. the PR currently points to the old qprofile anchor which 404s.

claire: exact. add a short note: "quant profile = lower precision for tokens after prefix to save memory" and link to /optimize/quant-profiles (new slug).

samir: draft snippet (python) — keeps it intentionally minimal:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(
  model="redwood-optimized-7b",
  prompt="Summarize the query",
  batching={"enabled": True, "max_batch_ms": 20},
  kv_prefetch={"enabled": True, "max_prefetch_tokens": 512},
  quant_profile="latency-tier-2",
  stream=False
)
print(resp.text)
```

samir: and a short Go example to mirror the options:
```go
// pseudo
c := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
opts := redwood.GenerateOptions{
  Model: "redwood-optimized-7b",
  Batching: map[string]interface{}{"enabled": true, "max_batch_ms": 20},
  KVPfetch: map[string]interface{}{"enabled": true, "max_prefetch_tokens": 512},
  QuantProfile: "latency-tier-2",
}
res, _ := c.Generate(ctx, "Summarize the query", opts)
fmt.Println(res.Text)
```

leo: these look good. please add a 2-line explanation under each snippet: why the values, expected perf impact, and an example of when to prefer stronger quantization (e.g., when throughput > 5k req/s and small accuracy hit is ok).

claire: also add a small "quick checks" section for engineers migrating: 
- run `make docs-linkcheck` locally
- ensure qprofile slug exists and points to the table
- run the sample with `REDWOOD_KEY` and check server logs for "kv-prefetch: hit_rate" metric

samir: adding. tagging @leo for the metrics line and where to point the link to the quant table.

leo: for the link, use /optimize/quant-profiles#profile-table — I created the anchor in the staging doc already. I'll push that anchor to the branch in a followup.

docs-bot: Linkcheck result: 1 broken link found in /docs/optkit/migrate.md -> http://old.docs/quant-tables (404). CI job id: 7890.

claire: perfect. once the anchor is pushed we can retarget the link. samir, can you add a small migration note about the config key rename (`kv_prefetch.max_tokens` -> `kv_prefetch.max_prefetch_tokens`)? devs hit this earlier.

samir: noted. will add a short note and a two-line backward compatibility snippet showing old->new mapping.

claire: timeline: if we can get this in today we can unblock the release. please add tests: 1) linkcheck passes 2) code sample lints (pyflakes or go vet).

samir: will do. PR update incoming in ~2 hrs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

leo: ping me when ready, I'll validate the metrics and the quant anchor.

claire: thanks team! small ask: keep snippets < 25 lines and avoid complex error handling so copy-paste works for users. :thumbsup:
